style_catalog.description: A source-led exploration of historic Cape farmstead composition, gables, roof forms, plastered masonry and sheltered stoep/threshold relationships. Use as a historically situated reference, not a universal regional template or climate-performance shortcut.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: Historical reference only. Interpret with local evidence, material context and heritage review; do not claim a single pure or timeless Cape identity.
must_not_assume: authenticity from location or resident identity

style_catalog.description: A historically layered Cape vernacular reference for Georgian-influenced symmetry, classical ordering and internal/external detailing. Treat it as one influence in an evolving tradition, not as a uniform standalone regional style.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: The source describes Georgian influence as one shift within Cape vernacular development; retain the specific reference and historical context.
must_not_assume: a single canonical Cape Georgian form

style_catalog.description: An exploratory family spanning varied Victorian-era compositions, rooflines, bays, verandahs and decorative detail. Select specific place, period and building precedents rather than treating the label as one universal recipe.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A broad historical family; exact regional variants and heritage significance require source context.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory early-20th-century family often associated with lighter classical detailing, generous openings and transitional domestic forms. Ground any use in a specific regional precedent and building type.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: Historical exploration only; features vary significantly by place, class, climate and period.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language of ordered composition, proportion, symmetry and classical references. Distinguish Georgian traditions from later Neoclassical revivals and identify the precedent being interpreted.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A broad family label, not a substitute for period-specific architectural research.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language emphasizing visible making, integrated joinery, tactile materials, human-scaled detail and craft-led composition. Material sourcing, durability and embodied impacts remain separately qualified.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: Craft language is not proof of local provenance, fair labour or repairability.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language of flowing lines, organic ornament, integrated metalwork, glass and crafted motifs. Separate decorative intent from fabrication, fire, safety and maintenance requirements.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A broad international family with distinct regional expressions.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language associated with horizontal composition, integrated spatial sequences, sheltering eaves and a deliberate relationship between building and landscape. Actual solar, wind and water performance require site analysis.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A historical movement, not a climate-neutral design prescription.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language connecting functional organization, geometric clarity, modern materials and the integration of art, craft and industrial production. Specific precedents and construction systems must be identified.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: Historical reference, not a synonym for generic minimalism or low-cost construction.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language of rationalized volumes, planar composition, structural expression and extensive glazing in some variants. Envelope, glare, overheating, privacy and energy consequences must be tested rather than inferred.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A historically diverse movement; avoid copying form without adapting to local context.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory family of restrained composition, daylight-conscious interiors, tactile materials and functional simplicity. Translate the actual principles to local climate and culture; do not import cold-climate assemblies by appearance.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A broad regional family with substantial variation across countries, periods and designers.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory family of arcades, courtyards, plastered surfaces, roof forms and layered thresholds. Select a specific region and historical lineage; avoid flattening colonial and postcolonial histories into a decorative kit.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: Regional variants and colonial histories differ; use source-led interpretation and context review.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory family of pitched roof forms, expressed timber, deep eaves and sheltered outdoor edges. Snow, wind, rain, fire, timber durability and structural loading are site-specific engineering questions.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A regionally situated precedent, not a generic roof or structure specification.

style_catalog.description: An exploratory language using layered references, symbolic form, historical quotation, colour and deliberate contrast. Meaning is resident- and context-dependent; no universal cultural or semantic score is assigned.
style_catalog.authenticity_note: A diverse movement; specify the intended precedent, motifs and meaning in the resident's own terms.

composition_model.description: Style families are architectural-expression references only. They do not define spatial typology, construction assemblies, environmental performance or experience feasibility.

regional_reference_modules.historical_scope: Documented nineteenth-century corbelled structures; not a generic contemporary house style.
regional_reference_modules.description: A heritage and research reference for the specific corbelled structures of the Great Karoo. Use for documentation, conservation, interpretation and carefully reviewed adaptation studies only; do not turn it into a new-build kit or infer a single cultural ownership.
regional_reference_modules.attribution_guardrail: UCT research describes frontier interactions and contested/multiple heritage claims. Any project-level interpretation requires exact asset provenance, local community engagement, rights review and qualified conservation input.
